utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Have the accused brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon to the interpreters. I'm making sure that everybody can hear me. Good afternoon to Prosecution counsel and Defence. We are still in the Prosecutor's rebuttal. I'm saying this for the public gallery. This is now the end -- well, at least the last part, if not the end, the last part of this long trial. We'll now give the Prosecutor the floor for his rebuttal. I think we are coming to the end of that rebuttal. What is your schedule, Mr. Prosecutor? How is this week going to work out in respect of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. President. Good afternoon Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. We have one witness to present tomorrow. He will be a short witness. We have no additional witnesses to present to the Trial Chamber. Today we will be presenting a set of documents. My colleague and I will present approximately six or seven sets of documents. Tomorrow we have approximately two sets of documents and we will conclude our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Let me now ask the Defence whether we might hope that the end of your surrebuttal, Mr. Hayman, will be completed by the end of Friday. This is Monday afternoon. If we hear a witness from the Prosecution tomorrow, you could begin when, and how long would your surrebuttal last?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Based on what has been presented so far in the Prosecution rebuttal case, Mr. President, the Defence believes it can complete its surrebuttal to that component of the rebuttal case this week. We don't know, however, what is coming in the "sets" of documents that my friend and colleague referred to. We don't know what they are. We don't know what it may surrebut those materials, if it's necessary to do so, in our judgement. So we cannot say yet, Mr. President, exactly what the parameters will be, but so far we have not seen anything that we believe will throw us of off schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you can, you would try to finish by 1.30 on Friday. If you can. If necessary, we'll extend the time. Thank you. We now turn to the Prosecutor for the presentation of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would raise one issue with the Trial Chamber, and that is the issue of notification. The Prosecutor has complied with the orders of this Court to notify the Defence of the names of witnesses and the substance of their testimony. To date we have not received any notification that the Defence intends to call any witnesses, and if they are intending to call witnesses, we would ask that the Court order them to notify us today of the names of those witnesses so we can have the benefit of the notice that we have accorded them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps that's because the Defence doesn't intend to call any witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We don't have a present intent right now to call any surrebuttal witnesses. We don't know if any witnesses may be necessary in terms of responding to material that has yet to arrive at our door. We will, Mr. President, if we form that intent to call a witness, we will give prompt notice along the lines, the format, that the parties have adhered to, to the Prosecutor, but we have to have a chance to see what it is first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But notification was supposed to take place how long before the presentation of the witness? I don't remember. What was the amount of time. Mr. Fourmy, can you help me, please? Mr. Hayman is saying that if he intends to present witnesses ... Seven days. Yes, thank you, Mr. Dubuisson. How are you going to work, Mr. Hayman? If you say that -- if we present surrebuttal witnesses - there are no hearings next week - I think those were times given to you in order to draft your briefs. How are things going to work?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the schedule is such that we're hearing part of the rebuttal case more than seven days before, or approximately seven days before, the commencement of the surrebuttal is scheduled, but we're hearing parts of the Prosecution rebuttal case less than seven days before the date on which our surrebuttal is scheduled to begin. If we feel we have to call a witness in response to something that has yet been presented in the Prosecutor's rebuttal case, then it is a physical impossibility. It is a mathematical impossibility, if the Court wishes us to present that witness on Thursday or Friday of this week, to give seven days' advance notice of that witness. Indeed, it may be a physical impossibility to get any such witness here on such short notice. We don't know because we don't know what witness that might be to respond to the documents that we have not yet seen or perhaps to respond to the testimony from Major Morsink that we have not yet heard. What I've said is, we will give prompt notice, same-day notice, to the Prosecutor if we form an intent, and, of course, we'll advise the Court if we're in session, or advise your staff if we're not in session, if we form an intent to call a witness in our surrebuttal. Now, the seven-day notice was the Court's rule. The Court is free to be flexible in these final stages of the case and we'll respect the Court's wishes, but it's a physical impossibility for us to give seven days' notice to respond to evidence that has not been presented if we are to present our response this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. At least we agree on one point, Mr. Hayman, that is, that since rebuttal has begun, we're working in different sequences. The Judges have a certain degree of autonomy in making decisions in that area. We will see where things stand either at the end of today or tomorrow at the end of the rebuttal. I think that would be best, Mr. Harmon. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is now 2.45. You can have the floor in order to present your documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. The first document I will be presenting is a binder. I've given those to the Registrar already. When he distributes these binders, I will explain what is contained within them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The binder will be 757.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will explain this document, Mr. President and Your Honours. There is, attached at the front of this document, an index of 50 pages. It is divided into three sections. The first section is found at the first page, and it is a document that has previously been admitted into evidence. It is an extraction from the Nadrodni List and it deals with confidential defence data and procedures for their protection. The second section of this document is found on page 3, and again, the theme is HVO communications. The second part, running from page 3 until page 15, has a sampling of HVO documents dealing with encryption capabilities and codes, the use of codes by the HVO. Section 3 of this document, starting on page 16 and running through the end of the document, consists of samples of orders by the HVO for communications equipment and invoices and shipping forms from the maintenance and repair depot in Travnik, showing delivery of certain types of equipment to the HVO in various municipalities that are mentioned in the indictment. This table is, as is stated at page 16, does not reflect nor is it intended to reflect all the different types of communication equipment that was available to the HVO or is it intended to represent the total volume of communications equipment that was available to the HVO in each of the municipalities. Tab number 22 is interesting because this is a document that deals with the organisation of communications in the JNA and the SFRY, and it describes in that document the various types of communications equipment, some of which is found in the ensuing tabs of this exhibit. From tab 23 on, one will see, for example, the delivery to the HVO of mobile telephones, radio set, communications vehicles of the TAM sort, et cetera. So this is, Mr. President, an exhibit, consisting, as I say, of 99 pages, dealing with the theme of HVO communications. The second set of documents, Mr. President, deals with General Blaskic's testimony about the attack on Stari Vitez that occurred on the 18th of July. You may recall that General Blaskic testified that on the 18th of July, he was in Busovaca attending a holy mass and he was having lunch with a parish priest, and at page 19484 of the transcript, starting at line 4 through line 7, Colonel Blaskic testified that -- previously he had testified that he was surprised by this attack and did not learn of it until he returned from Busovaca. At page 19498 at line 4, he says:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this attack, we had many casualties in the HVO, that is, the special purpose unit did, and I was informed that somewhere between 13 and 14 -- 13 to 15 soldiers had been killed. It is the Prosecutor's view that this was not an attack that was solely the result of Vitezovi activity but that multiple units engaged in this attack. The next exhibits, Mr. President, are a series of exhibits dealing with notification of death and wounding for various units of the HVO, including the military police, including the HVO home guard units and the like, and I'll pass these out one at a time, Mr. President. If I could have the assistance of the usher? There are six documents in this set.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 758, that is, the one that has 18 November, 1994, and it's 1423/94.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This, Mr. President and Your Honours, is a document dated the 18th of November, 1994, reflecting that this particular soldier was wounded on the 18th of July, 1993, and he is a member of the 92nd Regiment of the 3rd Battalion. That can be seen in the upper left-hand corner. The next document ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 759, which is dated 24 January, 1996, and it is 1779-09-96-926.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This document, Mr. President and Your Honours, indicates that a soldier, who is named in the document, was killed on the 18th of July at the Mahala in Stari Vitez. He was a member of the 92nd Viteska Home Guard Regiment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 760, 14 December, 1994. This is 1545/94.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. President and Your Honours, that indicates that the named individual in this document, who is a member of the 92nd Regiment of the 3rd Battalion, was wounded in the Stari Vitez area, and that's on the 18th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 761, 10 January, 1996. This is 1730-1/96-92.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. President and Your Honours, that indicates on the 18th of July, 1993, the named individual was a member of the 4th Vitez Military Police Battalion and he was killed in Vitez on the 18th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 762, 16 October, 1995. This is 1779-09.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document that indicates that the named individual, who was a member of the Vitez Regiment, was wounded on the 18th of July, 1993, and is signed by Mario Cerkez. The last document ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 763, in handwriting 17 December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This document, Mr. President and Your Honours, is a report of a wounding indicating that on the 18th of July, 1993, this particular individual was wounded in an attack on the Mahala. It is signed for the command of the Fifth Battalion. And that concludes this series of documents, Mr. President. Our next document, Mr. President, is a newspaper article from the publication Le Monde. It is dated the 5th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 764.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. President and Your Honours, entitled "The Croat-Muslim Conflict in Central Bosnia." It is from the special correspondent in Vitez from Le Monde, and on page 3 of the translation, the top paragraph references the ultimatum that has been at issue in this case, an ultimatum that expired on the 15th of April followed by the fighting the following morning of the 16th. Just so the record is clear and for counsel's recordkeeping purposes, the documents that deal with the wounding of the individuals and the killings of the individuals on the 18th of July were seized pursuant to a search warrant that was issued by the ICTY. The next document we have, Mr. President, is a citizenship certificate from the Republic of Croatia showing that Tihomir Blaskic is a Croatian citizen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 765.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The last document I am going to present, Mr. President, before yielding the floor to my colleague, Mr. Kehoe, is a document which is dated the 21st of November, 1995, and it is a decision on appointing General Blaskic to the post of Inspector in the Chief Inspectorate of the Croatian army, and the document is sealed and -- over the seal of Dr. Franjo Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 766.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, I'll yield the floor to Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. In conjunction with the documents relating to the communication capabilities of the HVO as presented by my colleague, we would also like to present a series of documents that were presented in large part, barring two, from the Croatian side of the Federation. If I may, Mr. Usher? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 767.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the exception of number 12 and number 13 in this set of documents in 767, all of these orders or requests for the British battalion to take Blaskic and others either from Vitez to Kiseljak or from Kiseljak to Vitez and Busovaca were given to the Office of the Prosecutor pursuant to a binding order by the Ministry of Defence, or the Federation side of the Ministry of Defence, and specifically the Croat side. Your Honours, when you review these documents, you will see where are the times and places of Blaskic's and other HVO personnel's travel between Kiseljak and Vitez and vice versa and the particular times that those took place. Again, we don't maintain that these are the only times that Blaskic did or could have got to Kiseljak, these are simply the ones that were produced to the Office of the Prosecutor by the HVO side of the Federation. The next set of documents, Mr. President, has to do with the home guards and the existence of the home guards, and in a series of questions not only in response to the Prosecutor but also in response to questions by Judge Rodrigues, the accused maintained that there were no home guards and that they were not fully established. I would like to offer a series of documents concerning the home guards, if I may? It is a series of ten documents. It might be easier, Mr. Registrar, to just number that -- we'll go through each document in sequence, because they are not to be taken as a bundle, just one after the other, similar to what Mr. Harmon just did. So if we could take it from 768, 769? The first document would be 768, which is a document of the 5th of February, 1993, signed by Bruno Stojic, the Minister of Defence, ordering the establishment of the home guards. Document 768 was a document that was seized pursuant to a search warrant signed by the Tribunal. The next document is document 769, dated 8 February, 1993, an order of Milivoj Petkovic to implement the order of Bruno Stojic and establish the home guards. This document was obtained from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The next document is a plan for setting up the municipal home guard and home guard's command, dated in Vitez March 1993. There is one copy for Vares and another for Kakanj. They are exactly the same documents and they are signed by the accused, Tihomir Blaskic. That was obtained from the Bosnian government.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 770.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. The next document -- sorry. The next document, Your Honours and counsel, is an order of the accused dated 11 March, 1993, again reiterating an order on the setting up of the home guards. That would be document 771, and this document was a document that was seized pursuant to a search warrant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could you give us the page of the transcript where the accused's statement is found, that was given as a sworn statement? Could you give us the page number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the entire page sequence dealing with the home guards goes from page 21983 to 22903. That includes various questions. On page 22898, we talked about two documents, and the question was asked on line 24 of page 22898: "Q. Did the home guard units, the Domobrani, exist in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the home guards did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there a corps of command or did you have an assistant for the home guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were in the stage we had determined and appointed commanders for the home guard units and in the process of establishing the home guard units, but the war with the BH army in the spring of 1993 stopped us in this process and we were not able to implement that project, that is to say, we never actually organised and formed the home guard units."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to consult with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the Judges consider it appropriate to ask you whether you consider that there was a false testimony on the part of the accused who, at the time, was under oath. This is the question that the Judges are asking you. This is the question that the Judges are asking. They are asking whether you intend to maintain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, on numerous various issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. At what point will you do that? Will that be later?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think regarding the fallacious testimony of the accused, the prevarications of the accused, we will, of course, discuss those in our post-trial brief that we will be filing on the 22nd, and then, of course, there will be significant discussion on that score during final argument, but rest assured that given the testimony not only during the Prosecution case but also during the Court witnesses that Your Honours called, that the issue of the accused's credibility is very much in issue and very much on the table and we challenge that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The Judges thank you for your answer. You may now proceed. You may proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. The next document is a document again concerning the home guards. This is 772, a document of the 12th of March, 1993, listing three individuals that were proposed as the temporary home guard commanders, and this is signed by the head of the Defence Department from Travnik, Marijan Skopljak. The next two documents are documents that we will place in evidence at 773 and 774. These two documents signed by Zvonko Vukovic place the command of the home guards under the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The document at 16.30, 774, gives immediate orders to the home guards to conduct round-the-clock inspections or introduce round-the-clock duties and other matters.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 773, that is, the document from 15.30; and 774, which was for 16.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next document is a document that is dated the 16th of March, 1993. This, of course, would be document 775. It is an order from Zvonko Vukovic to immediately have the home guard commanders come to a meeting at the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone at 11.00 on the 17th of March, 1993. That document, 775, was obtained pursuant to a search warrant. Document 776 is a document that is dated the 23rd of March, 1993, which has a list of individuals with their pedigrees attached. It is directed to the assistant commander of the home guard for Vitez and is signed by Marijan Skopljak. I would indicate to Your Honours, in this document as well as in document 772, they both mention an individual by the name of Nenad Santic who, of course, was very prominently mentioned during the attacks in the Santici and Ahmici area. The last document in this array is a document signed by -- I don't believe it's signed but someone signed on behalf of the accused, from the 1st of April, 1993, at 11.10, and notes that given the fact that orders on the formation of the home guards have not been carried out, and he asked for more rapid deployment, and then he calls upon a -- requesting information from the home guards as well as setting up a meeting on the 6th of April, 1993, where he notes at that meeting that commanders will assume command of their particular home guard units and receive letters of appointments and other documents. That document, for consistency, is document 777. Mr. President, that is the last document in the sequence of the home guard documents. I would like to return to the testimony of a different witness, not the accused, but a witness that I'm sure Your Honours can recall, and it was Dr. Bilandzic, Dr. Dusan Bilandzic, who testified in September of last year before Your Honour, Judge Rodrigues, joined us. If Your Honours recall, during the testimony of Dr. Bilandzic, an issue was raised concerning an interview that Dr. Bilandzic had with Nacional, where he discussed this meeting with the Serbs where they looked at maps and hashed out various issues regarding the division of Bosnia. This meeting, of course, was on the heels of the meeting between Milosevic and Tudjman in Karadjordjevo. Without going into all of the details of that interview which, of course, are in Prosecutor's Exhibit 464, Your Honours will recall that Dr. Bilandzic, on cross-examination, said that he retracted a significant portion of that, and his retraction, which is Exhibit 465, he noted: "The interview did not distort the essence of what he said," but he said his entire retraction was not published in Nacional. What we have, Mr. President, is Nacional's response that they published once -- the testimony of Dr. Bilandzic was brought before this Court, and Nacional issued an editorial, if I may present it to Your Honours, commenting on exactly what happened during the interview with Dr. Bilandzic. While we're waiting, Mr. President, and bringing this before the Registrar, I know Your Honour wants of the actual pagination of the discussion with Dr. Bilandzic, and the pages where these matters were discussed with Dr. Bilandzic focus page 11401 and incorporate 11411. I will note that Judge Shahabuddeen's questions on this matter begin again 11464 and just on to 11466. My memory doesn't serve me correctly, but I think they were questions, Your Honour, that you asked at the end as the pagination sequence from the cross doesn't follow, but I think that's what happened. In this particular document, which is an editorial board article that was published by Nacional, there is discussion about the particular article that appeared in Nacional, Exhibit 464; the retraction, Exhibit 465, and this Nacional article reflects that Professor Bilancic was given the opportunity to read his initial article before it was published, that he never actually retracted much of the things that he says he retracted, specifically the conversation between him and Tudjman, where Tudjman noted that the Muslims would have to go along with the Serb-Croat division of Bosnia. I place this document in the record but just go to the penultimate paragraph in this particular article by Nacional, where the article -- or the editorial board of Nacional reflects as follows: "Having analysed Dusan Bilandzic's testimony in The Hague, the editorial board of Nacional, including three editors who were present in 1996 when Bilandzic vigorously and convincingly described the talks on carving up Bosnia-Herzegovina, still firmly defends the authenticity of his interview to Nacional of 25 October, 1996." So this document not only does that but also reflects that Dr. Bilandzic was given the opportunity to read the initial article and also given the opportunity to read his retraction. So we offer that into evidence to complete the picture concerning Dr. Bilandzic's testimony. I do believe, Mr. President, that at this point, looking for more paper around here, just making sure that we've covered it all, heaven knows we were discussing how this case is a threat to the trees of America and the rest of Europe, but I do believe that we are done with the paper for today, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This was a threat for the American forest, Mr. Kehoe, and I suppose it could also be a threat for the Judges' health.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely. I didn't leave out the European forest as well, Judge. I'm sure it's just for every tree around. I do believe that is all we have at this juncture, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the transcript, I want to be sure that the article in Nacional is 768 -- 778. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. If that's what you have to say, we're going to adjourn and we will resume at 10.00 tomorrow morning to hear your witness. You will then be finished with your rebuttal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: at 3.27 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 6th day of July, 1999 at 10:00 a.m.
